ledger.note: c. 1521: Golconda extends south and south-east over about 193 cells (lat 15.9-17.6 N, lon 77.8-82.3 E) that Cliopatria takes from Vijayanagara in 1521. The Quli Qutb Shah page names the land without years: 'Sultan Quli extended his rule by capturing forts at Warangal, Kondapalli, Eluru, and Rajamundry', the fort of Khammam, and says he 'forced Jeypore's ruler Vishwanath Dev Gajapati to surrender all the territories'; the Gajapati page says that 'By the early 16th century, the Gajapatis lost great portions of their southern dominion to the Vijayanagara Empire and the Golconda Sultanate' (no year). So the east of the shape is former Gajapati land taken by Quli, not clearly Vijayanagara's; Cliopatria's Vijayanagara counterpart is kept, and the 1521 year is Cliopatria's. Vijayanagara's Krishnadevaraya had fought Sultan Quli at Pangal in 1513 (Quli page). The Gajapati kingdom has no dossier yet (sa-04-x).

notes: Golconda (9 Cliopatria shapes, 1519-1686): five of the eight shape changes (1521, 1572, 1612 gains; 1659 loss; 1640 gain) are Cliopatria's and no page opened dates or names them; they are confidence-1 bridges and the keyframes carry 'unverified: page budget'. The Qutb Shahi page gives no area, no Vijayanagara or Gajapati conquests, and no capital years. A gap-filler should open 'Hyderabad' or 'Golconda Fort' for the capital, and 'Kondavidu', 'Rajahmundry' and the Gajapati/Orissa articles for the 1521, 1572 and 1612 gains. Mir Jumla II's page dates Golconda's Carnatic conquests (1642, 1646-47, 1650) which fall south of the Cliopatria shape; the 1640 keyframe adds them. The tributary submission of the Kingdom of Chandragiri in April 1647 is not entered as a vassal_start because no page dates its end. The Mughal dossier (sa-05) should carry: a vassal relation of Golconda from 1636 ('Shah Jahan forced the Qutb Shahis to recognize Mughal suzerainty'), a gain from Golconda in 1656-1659 (northern strip) and the annexation of September 1687. The Qutb Shahi table dates Sultan Quli's rule from 1512, the Quli page from 7 December 1518; the dossier starts in December 1518. The place name Gandikota is not in the gazetteer. 'Kingdom of Chandragiri' and 'Timma Nayadu (Gandikota)' have no dossier (counterparts_needing_dossiers). || FIX PASS 2026-10-19 (after the adversarial review): (1) vassal_start 1636 for mughal-empire added (Qutb Shahi page, re-read); it runs to the 1687 dissolve. (2) The 1640-1658 keyframe is split: 1640-1641 is the 1640 shape without the Nellore-Udayagiri-Gandikota lands, which enter in 1642, 1646 and 1650 (new keyframes); the shapes of 1659-1687 keep those lands because the ledger never loses them, and the 1687 loss and dissolve use that shape. I disagree with the reviewer on one point: the 123 cells Cliopatria adds in 1640 are not the Nellore and Gandikota lands (only 27 lie in the Nellore circle; the other 96, round 16 N 79-80 E, are Guntur-Palnadu), so those 96 are kept from 1640 as a confidence-1 event instead of being dropped. (3) The 1642 counterpart is now 'Kingdom of Chandragiri', as in 1646 (the Mir Jumla page names no 1642 defender). (4) Thin items re-checked: the Quli Qutb Shah and Gajapati pages name the land of the 1521 gain (Warangal, Kondapalli, Eluru, Rajamundry, Khammam; Gajapati territories) but no year; the 1572 and 1612 coastal gains are Cliopatria's (the Gajapati page ends their rule in 1541); the Abdullah Qutb Shah page lists no ceded land for 1656-1659; the Hyderabad page says Hyderabad was founded in 1591 'to extend the capital' without saying the court moved. (5) Gandikota is written as {lon 78.28, lat 14.81, km 60} throughout because the gazetteer lacks the name (it was a place term before); the name is still reported under gazetteer_names_needed.
